name: Dow

summary.text: Dow is a Michigan-based chemical and plastics producer. An NPR and PBS Frontline investigation published in September 2020, based on internal industry documents and interviews with former officials, reported that plastics makers knew for years that recycling plastic was not economically viable while spending millions promoting it. A 1989 document described in the report called executives from Exxon, Chevron, Amoco, Dow, DuPont, Procter & Gamble and others to a private meeting in Washington as the industry's image deteriorated.

sources.title: How Big Oil Misled The Public Into Believing Plastic Would Be Recycled

facts.claim: NPR and PBS Frontline reported in September 2020 that the nation's largest oil and gas companies, as the makers of plastic, knew for years that recycling plastic was not valuable while spending millions telling the public the opposite.

openQuestions: Site claim (documented; industry doubted recycling from the 1970s yet promoted it): supported by NPR's reporting; the 1970s dating comes from documents described in the full NPR piece, not in the excerpts in the sources used.

The trade group employing 'Thomas' (reported elsewhere as the Society of the Plastics Industry) was not confirmed from the excerpts; the site entity 'plastics-industry-trade-groups' could be linked once confirmed.
Dow-specific statements about recycling were not found.
